cards.text: Paul, an apostle, is writing to the churches of Galatia (Galatians 1:1-2). He just finished saying a person is justified by faith in Christ, not by works of the law (Galatians 2:16). Now he turns to them, and friend, he does NOT warm up first: "O foolish Galatians! Who has bewitched you?"

cards.question: Paul reminds the Galatians of something they already saw. What was clearly portrayed before their very eyes?

cards.text: Then Paul says he'd like to learn just one thing from the Galatians. ONE thing. Friend, when a coworker says "just one quick question," clear your whole afternoon.

cards.question: Paul asks if the Galatians received the Spirit by works of the law or by hearing with faith. True or false: Paul is pointing them to hearing with faith.

cards.text: And that one thing turns into another: "Are you so foolish? After starting in the Spirit, are you now finishing in the flesh?"

cards.question: Paul asks if the Galatians are now finishing in the flesh after starting in the Spirit. What's his point?

answers.text: They changed course from how they began
They are moving too slowly to finish
They should start over under the law

cards.text: Then Paul asks if they've suffered so much for nothing, if it really was for nothing.

cards.question: Paul asks if God lavishes His Spirit on the Galatians, and does something else among them, because they practice the law or because they hear and believe. What else does God do among them?

cards.text: Then Paul goes ALL the way back to Abraham, the man God called to leave his country (Genesis 12:1). Paul quotes Genesis 15:6 about him.

cards.question: Abraham ___ God, and it was credited to him as righteousness.
Paul tells the Galatians to understand what that means. Who does he say are the sons of Abraham?

answers.text: Those born in his family line

cards.text: Paul says the Scripture foresaw that God would justify the Gentiles by faith, and foretold the gospel to Abraham.

cards.question: The Scripture foretold the gospel to Abraham: all ___ will be blessed through you.

cards.text: So Paul lands it: those who have faith are blessed along with Abraham, the man of faith.
Now Paul flips the coin over. What about everybody who relies on works of the law?

cards.question: Paul says all who rely on works of the law are under a ___.

cards.text: And Paul doesn't just SAY it, friend. He pulls out the receipts and quotes Deuteronomy 27:26.

cards.question: Paul quotes what is written: cursed is everyone who does not continue to do how much of what's written in the Book of the Law?
Paul says no one is justified before God by the law, and he quotes Habakkuk 2:4: the righteous will live by ___.

cards.text: Then Paul puts the law and faith side by side, friend, and takes a hard look at the law.

cards.question: Paul compares the law and faith. True or false: he says the law is based on faith.

cards.text: The law runs on doing: "The man who does these things will live by them." Friend, I can't finish ONE batch without a chocolate chip hitting the floor, so I am SO glad Paul brings in a rescue next.

cards.question: Who does Paul say redeemed us from the curse of the law?
How does Paul say Christ redeemed us from the curse of the law?

answers.text: By becoming a curse for us

cards.text: Paul quotes Deuteronomy 21:23: "Cursed is everyone who is hung on a tree."

cards.question: Paul says why Christ redeemed us. True or false: it was so the blessing promised to Abraham would come to the Gentiles in Christ Jesus.
Christ redeemed us so that by faith we might receive the promise of the ___.
